title: Composition Candidates To Add
description: New compositions (frameworks, services, protocols, applications) surfaced during scans or pattern authoring but not yet catalogued in compositions-src/. The symmetric analog of pattern-todo.json for the composition layer. Distinct from compositions-todo.json (a pattern-centric usage-coverage worklist). Each entry names a candidate composition, the patterns it would implement, and the upstream evidence with a verifiable url and verbatim quote. needs_verification:true means the candidate was surfaced from a secondary mention and must have its own primary source content-verified before authoring. Entries graduate by being authored into compositions-src/ and removed from this list.

candidates.name: verl (Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning for LLMs)
candidates.summary: ByteDance's open-source RL post-training library for LLMs and the de-facto substrate for agentic RL: multi-turn rollouts with tool calling, agent loops, PPO/GRPO/GSPO/DAPO/PRIME, vLLM/SGLang rollout engines against FSDP/Megatron training engines, and an explicit 'zero-mismatch' rollout path built on batch-invariant kernels. Wave 1 claimed OpenEnv, verifiers and the Prime Intellect Environments Hub (the environment side); verl is the training-loop side of the same stack and is not yet claimed.

candidates.name: CHESS
candidates.summary: A four-agent text-to-SQL framework (Information Retriever, Schema Selector, Candidate Generator, Unit Tester) that decomposes NL-to-SQL over enterprise-scale catalogs into value retrieval, schema pruning, iterative candidate generation, and LLM-written natural-language unit tests over the generated query.

evidence.title: CHESS: Contextual Harnessing for Efficient SQL Synthesis
evidence.quote: We introduce CHESS, a Large Language Model (LLM) based multi-agent framework for efficient and scalable SQL synthesis, comprising four specialized agents, each targeting one of the aforementioned challenges: the Information Retriever (IR) extracts relevant data, the Schema Selector (SS) prunes large schemas, the Candidate Generator (CG) generates high-quality candidates and refines queries iteratively, and the Unit Tester (UT) validates queries through LLM-based natural language unit tests.

candidates.name: HAL (Holistic Agent Leaderboard)

Catalog already has inspect-ai, braintrust, langsmith, arize-phoenix, langfuse, promptfoo, ragas and deepeval, but no leaderboard-grade agent harness that treats cost and log auditing as first-class.

evidence.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
evidence.quote: First, we provide a standardized evaluation harness that orchestrates parallel evaluations across hundreds of VMs, reducing evaluation time from weeks to hours while eliminating common implementation bugs.

evidence.title: Holistic Agent Leaderboard: The Missing Infrastructure for AI Agent Evaluation
evidence.quote: We validate the harness by conducting 21,730 agent rollouts across 9 models and 9 benchmarks in coding, web navigation, science, and customer service with a total cost of about $40,000.

evidence.title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A
evidence.quote: We introduce Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens (IBCTs), a primitive that fuses identity, attenuated authorization, and provenance binding into a single append-only token chain.

candidates.name: Open Agent Passport (OAP)

evidence.title: Before the Tool Call: Deterministic Pre-Action Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
evidence.quote: We characterize this gap as the pre-action authorization problem and present the Open Agent Passport (OAP), an open specification and reference implementation that intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution, evaluates them against a declarative policy, and produces a cryptographically signed audit record.

candidates.name: ROSClaw (OpenClaw ROS 2 executive layer)

Deployed on wheeled, quadruped and humanoid platforms with four model backends; also used as a measurement instrument, finding up to 4.8x variation in out-of-policy action proposal rates between backends. The catalog currently has no robotics/embodied composition at all.

evidence.title: ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction
evidence.quote: We present ROSClaw, a model-agnostic executive layer that integrates the OpenClaw agent runtime with ROS 2, enabling any foundation model to perceive, reason about, and act on any ROS-enabled robot through (i) dynamic capability discovery with standardized affordance injection, (ii) multimodal observation normalization, (iii) pre-execution action validation within a configurable safety envelope, and (iv) structured audit logging.

candidates.name: Progent
candidates.summary: Privilege-control layer for tool-using LLM agents (UC Berkeley). A domain-specific policy language of symbolic rules over tool names and arguments is generated from the user's task, deterministically checked on every tool call, and revised during execution under an SMT expansion check so privileges can only narrow without approval. Integrates without altering agent internals; used as a comparison baseline and independently reproduced on AgentDojo by third parties.

evidence.title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control (arXiv:2504.11703)
evidence.quote: Thanks to its modular design, integrating Progent does not alter agent internals and requires only minimal changes to agent implementation.

evidence.title: Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents (arXiv:2606.26479)
evidence.quote: We then run that protocol as an independent reproduction and extension of Progent's own adaptive-attack analysis, on AgentDojo, with an open-weight agent (Qwen2.5-7B) self-hosted on a single H200, a setting its authors did not test.
